answer: Proof-of-personhood needs three signatures, and the pool rotates so no two signers share a subnet, a payout path, or an owner. A sonnet and a database migration get the same panel; the work type does not matter, only that the signers are unrelated. A pulse check before each signature fails closed if an endpoint is dead or duplicated, and the summit check voids the attestation when the panel turns out narrow. Three thousand real signers for a thousand fakes, and no farm owns them.
